name: Rogers Communications Inc.
moat_justification: Canadian telecom oligopoly member with the #1 wireless base, a national cable footprint after Shaw, deep spectrum holdings and unique sports/media assets; ROIC proxy stayed 10.2-16.2% over 2020-2025 (13.9% in 2025) and gross margin expanded from 42.1% to 45.2%, but the moat is shared with Bell/Telus, the regulator keeps prying at wholesale access, and population-driven subscriber growth is fading.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency CAD converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 40-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-06, accession 0000733099-26-000009), cover page: securities registered under Section 12(b) are 'Class B Non-Voting' shares, trading symbol RCI, listed on the New York Stock Exchange — the NYSE security is the Class B share itself, not an ADS; the same cover reports 111,152,011 Class A Voting and 429,073,267 Class B Non-Voting shares outstanding (540,225,278 total, vs the 541,000,000 diluted count the engine uses)) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 2.83 vs 3-yr median 1.98 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 27.0x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.5%) vs bull-case tier C (11.2%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Solid oligopoly cash machine, moat 6/10 — but at $31.99 the price already pays for the recovery: weighted IRR 9.3% on the normalized base (method range D to C) and it clears 15% only at or below the $17.28 weighted IV@15%.
moat_for: Regulated three-player oligopoly with foreign-ownership limits and spectrum scarcity
#1 wireless subscriber base; 66-67% wireless EBITDA margins, best-in-class churn (0.94-0.99% postpaid)
National cable/internet footprint from the 2023 Shaw acquisition plus deep spectrum holdings
ROIC proxy 10.2-16.2% across 2020-2025 and gross margin up from 42.1% to 45.2%
Sports/media assets no rival can replicate (Toronto Blue Jays, 75% of MLSE moving to 100%)
moat_against: Moat is shared: Bell and Telus hold comparable scale, spectrum and margins
CRTC wholesale/MVNO mandates and political pressure on consumer prices cap pricing power
Federal immigration cuts remove the population-growth tailwind behind subscriber adds
Quebecor/Freedom competes on price nationally since the Shaw deal remedies
Net debt of $29.0B (3.9x EBITDA) limits flexibility; cord-cutting erodes cable video
